# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.EndFree

/-!
# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)

**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex" (items
D.1–D.4), which `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` does not define (§75, Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are
§36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the administering value; `writeShared` alone is
insufficient), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities), §38 and §46 (library state outside
`S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the guard over all registries of live administrations)
and §58 (outcomes, statics before `fail`).

The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3).
`freeSlot` applies the effect function of O12 (§69) to the slot content under preconditions that
exempt `internal` and its ancestors (`ContentEndPre`): it is not a kernel `endUse` step.
`contentEnd_preserves` proves that it preserves `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57); `pstep_kernel` states what
every pool step is on the kernel side.
-/

namespace Ern.Lib.HandlePool

open Ern.MemoryModel
open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Library state (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §38, §46) -/

/-- Slot of a pool entry (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`;
non-normative library contract; §38, §46). -/
structure Slot where
  place : Nat
  gen : Nat
  live : Bool
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Pool entry `{storage, internal, slots}` with its logical identity (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1;
non-normative library contract). The pool value is the place holding `internal` (§46 analogue). -/
structure Pool where
  id : Nat
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  slots : List Slot
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Handle `(poolId, slot, gen)`: data, not an authority (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §37, §89;
non-normative library contract). -/
structure Handle where
  id : Nat
  slot : Nat
  gen : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Ghost record of a resolution (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; auxiliary information creating no
right, §38): pool identity and `internal`, the companion, the mode, and the entry authorities

+/-- An active authority with no origin is held by the owner of the root place of every leaf it
+covers (the converse of `RootHeld` restricted to active authorities), from `WF3` (§49.4, §49.7),

+theorem rootHeldConv_active {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (h1 : I1 s) (hnd : NoDangling s) :
+    ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.active = true →

+  obtain ⟨hlP, hleaf⟩ := hw.footprints x z hz l hl
+  have hlfr : l ∈ footprint s.P r := mem_footprint.2 ⟨hlP, hleaf, hlr⟩
+  have hur : s.Usable r := Decidable.byContradiction fun hu => hnd x z hz za r hu l hlfr hl
+  obtain ⟨i, z', pr, hz', za', zo', zm', hpr, hh', hfp'⟩ := hw.rootHeld r hr hur
+  by_cases hix : i = x
+  · subst hix; rw [hz] at hz'; cases hz'; exact ⟨pr, hpr, hh'⟩
+  · have hancs : ∀ j w, s.A[j]? = some w → w.origin = none → s.ancs j = [] :=
+      fun j w hj hw0 => by
+        have : s.org j = none := by simp [S3.org, hj, hw0]
+        simp [S3.ancs, chain_none this]
+    have := (h1 i x z' z l hix hz' hz za' za ((hfp' l).2 hlfr) hl

+    rw [zm'] at this; cases this

· exact hx

/-- The end of the content preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §69; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3), under
`WF3` (§49) and `RootHeldConv` (§40): an active authority on a leaf of a place that stops being
usable is derived, and blocked by §69.2 on dying storage, or a root, held by the owner of the root
place of the leaf, which stays usable. -/
theorem contentEnd_noDangling {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)
    (ha : RootHeldConv s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) (hw' : WF3 (endUseEff s q)) :
    NoDangling (endUseEff s q) := by
  have hU := EndFree.cleanup_usable (endUseS s q)
  intro j z hz za q' hq l hl hlz
  obtain ⟨hz₀, hnh, hlive⟩ := EndFree.endUse_active hz za
  by_cases hq₀ : ¬ s.Usable q'
  · exact hnd j z hz₀ za q' hq₀ l hl hlz
  replace hq₀ := Decidable.of_not_not hq₀
  obtain ⟨-, hleaf, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  have hl₀ : s.Usable l := usable_of_partOf hw (l + 1) l q' (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlq hq₀
  have hl₁ : ¬ (endUseS s q).Usable l := fun hu => hq (usable_of_part hw' hlq ((hU l).2 hu))
  cases hzo : z.origin with
  | some o =>
    have hacc := hpre.dying j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz₀))
    unfold DyingAccessOK OptP at hacc; rw [hz₀] at hacc
    rcases hacc za (by rw [hzo]; simp) ⟨l, hlz, hleaf, hl₀, hl₁⟩ with e | e
    · exact hnh e
    · exact e hlive
  | none =>
    obtain ⟨-, -, r, -, -, -, hr, hlr, -⟩ := hw.rootChain j z l hz₀ hlz hleaf
    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hh⟩ := ha j z l r hz₀ hzo hlz hr hlr
    have hnown : ¬ OwnedIn s.P q r := fun hown => by
      cases hown with
      | @direct _ o _ hpl ho hpart =>
        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
        rw [hh, e] at hnh; exact hnh hpart
      | @step _ o _ hpl ho hown' =>
        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
        rw [hh, e] at hlive
        have := EndFree.dead_false hlive
        simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at this
        exact this.2 hown'
    have hd : (endUseS s q).dead r = false := by
      simp only [endUseS, ← hw.deadOf hlr, EndFree.dead_false hl₀, Bool.false_or,
        decide_eq_false_iff_not]
      exact hnown
    have hr₁ : (endUseS s q).Usable r := EndFree.usable_of_owner hpr hd (hh ▸ hlive)
    exact hl₁ ((hU l).1 (usable_of_partOf hw' (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlr ((hU r).2 hr₁)))

/-- The end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` preserves the kernel invariant
`KInv` (§57) and `KAux` (§40, §49.7) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la préservation des invariants
sous ce droit constitue une obligation explicite"; §69 effect). -/
theorem contentEnd_preserves {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s)
    (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) : KInv (endUseEff s q) ∧ KAux (endUseEff s q) := by
  have hw := hk.1
  refine ⟨EndFree.releases_preserve hk (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl rfl rfl
    (fun q h => by simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff] at h; exact h.1)
    (fun q' pl r hq hp => ?_) (fun q' _ x hx => ?_) (contentEnd_anchors hk.2.1.1.2.2.1 hpre)
    (fun r n z pr _ hur hz _ _ hpr hzh _ => ?_)
    (contentEnd_noDangling hw hk.2.1.2.2 ha hpre),
    EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux ha (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl⟩
  · obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, hd⟩ := hw.places q' pl r hq hp
    simp only [endUseS, hd, decide_eq_decide.2 (EndFree.ownedIn_parent hw hq hp)]
  · simp only [endUseS] at hx; split at hx
    · simp at hx
    · exact hx
  · have hnh : ¬ heldIn s.P q z.holder := fun hh => by
      have hd := EndFree.dead_false hur
      simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at hd
      rw [hzh] at hh
      cases ho : pr.owner with
      | frame f => rw [ho] at hh; exact hh
      | place o => rw [ho] at hh; exact hd.2 (.direct hpr ho hh)
    rw [EndFree.endUseS_get, hz]; simp [hnh]

  induction h₂ with
  | refl => exact h₁
  | tail _ hs ih => exact .tail ih hs

/-- One kernel step is a sequence (§57). -/
theorem KSeq.single {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : KStep k s s') : KSeq k s s' := .tail (.refl s) h

theorem releaseAll_kseq {k : K} : ∀ {s s' : S3} {l : List Nat}, releaseAll s l = some s' →
    KSeq k s s'
  | s, s', [], h => by simp only [releaseAll, Option.some.injEq] at h; subst h; exact .refl s
  | s, s', a :: l, h => by
    simp only [releaseAll] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i hpre
      exact (KSeq.single (.release (Guarded.ok hpre))).trans (releaseAll_kseq h)
    · cases h

/-- The `Observe` derivations of `resolveMany` are a sequence of `derive` steps (§60; HandlePool
v0.4 annex, D.2). -/
theorem derives_kseq {k : K} {c : Nat} : ∀ {s : S3} {rs : List (List Nat)}, DerivesPre s c rs →
    KSeq k s (derivesEff s c rs)
  | s, [], _ => .refl s
  | _, _ :: _, ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ => (KSeq.single (.derive (Guarded.ok h₁))).trans (derives_kseq h₂)

/-- The entry authorities of `resolveMany` are a `split` (§61) or a sequence of `derive` steps
(§60) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2). -/
theorem entries_kseq {k : K} {m : Mode} {s : S3} {c : Nat} {rs : List (List Nat)}
    (h : EntriesPre k m s c rs) : KSeq k s (entriesEff m s c rs) := by
  cases m with
  | modify => exact KSeq.single (.split (Guarded.ok h))
  | observe => exact derives_kseq h

/-- Under `KInv` (§57), exercisable `Modify` over a usable leaf gives the preconditions of an
ordinary write of that leaf (§67; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: the write of the handle). -/
theorem write_of_right {s : S3} (hk : KInv s) {dst : Nat} (hu : s.Usable dst)
    (hl : isLeaf s.P dst) (hr : HasRight s .modify dst) : ∃ a, Write3Pre s a [dst] := by
  obtain ⟨a, -, hex, hall⟩ := hr
  have hmem : dst ∈ footprint s.P dst := mem_footprint.2 ⟨hu.lt, hl, hu.lt, .inl rfl⟩
  have he : effective s a dst = some .modify := Arena.allows_modify_iff.1 (hall dst hmem)
  refine ⟨a, ⟨fun l hl' => ?_, hex, fun l hl' => ?_, fun l hl' b _ hb => ?_, fun l hl' => ?_⟩⟩
  · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hl']; exact ⟨dst, List.mem_range.2 hu.lt, hu, hmem⟩
  · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hl']; exact he
  · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hl']; exact effective_exclusive hk.2.1.1.1 (Ne.symm hb) he
  · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hl']
    exact fun q _ hq x hx => hk.2.1.1.2.2.1 q (usable_of_part hk.1 hq hu) x hx

/-- What a pool step is on the kernel side (HandlePool v0.4 annex; §57, §69): under `KInv`, every
step but `freeSlot` is a finite sequence of kernel steps O1–O16 (`newPool` none, `allocSlot` one
`write`, `resolve` two `derive`, `resolveMany` one `derive` then one `split` or one `derive` per
handle, `unresolve` `release` steps); `freeSlot` is the effect of O12 on the slot content under
`ContentEndPre`. -/
theorem pstep_kernel {k : K} {L L' : PState} (hk : KInv L.kern) (h : PStep k L L') :
    KSeq k L.kern L'.kern ∨
      ∃ q i, ContentEndPre k L.kern q i ∧ L'.kern = endUseEff L.kern q := by
  cases h with
  | kernel hs => exact .inl (KSeq.single hs)
  | newPool hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact .inl (.refl _)
  | allocSlot hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ hst _ _ =>
      obtain ⟨a, hw⟩ := write_of_right hk hst.dstUsable hst.dstLeaf hst.dstRight
      exact .inl (KSeq.single (.write (a := a) (Guarded.ok hw)))
  | resolve hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ hR _ _ hE =>
      exact .inl ((KSeq.single (.derive (Guarded.ok hR))).tail (.derive (Guarded.ok hE)))
  | resolveMany hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ hR _ hE => exact .inl ((KSeq.single (.derive (Guarded.ok hR))).trans (entries_kseq hE))
  | unresolve hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ hr => exact .inl (releaseAll_kseq hr)
  | freeSlot hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ _ _ _ hE => exact .inr ⟨_, _, hE, rfl⟩

/-- `XReach` is closed under sequences of kernel steps (§57). -/
theorem XReach.kseq {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s s' : S3} (hr : XReach k statics s)
    (h : KSeq k s s') : XReach k statics s' := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact hr
  | tail _ hs ih => exact .step ih (.kernel hs)

/-- The guarantee of §57 on the kernel side of library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex): `KInv` on
every state reached by kernel steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents. It is not a clause of the
contract and is not proved here: `xreach_inv` reduces it to the preservation of `KInv ∧ KAux` by
every kernel step, which the transfer of §63 breaks (`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
def KernelGuarantee (k : K) (statics : Statics) : Prop := ∀ s, XReach k statics s → KInv s

/-- A library step from a kernel state in `XReach` lands in `XReach`, under `KInv` (§57;
HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem xreach_pstep {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L L' : PState}
    (hr : XReach k statics L.kern) (hk : KInv L.kern) (hs : PStep k L L') :
    XReach k statics L'.kern := by
  rcases pstep_kernel hk hs with h | ⟨q, i, hpre, he⟩
  · exact hr.kseq h
  · rw [he]; exact .step hr (.contentEnd hpre)

/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is reached from `S3.init statics` by kernel
steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex), given `KInv` on such
states. -/
theorem pReach_xreach {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hX : KernelGuarantee k statics)
    {L : PState} (h : PReach k statics L) : XReach k statics L.kern := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ hs ih => exact xreach_pstep ih (hX _ ih) hs

/-- `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57) holds on every state reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents,
when it holds initially and every kernel step O1–O16 preserves it (`contentEnd_preserves` covers the
ends of slot contents; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem xreach_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (h0 : KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics))
    (hK : ∀ s s', KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∧ KAux s') {s : S3}
    (h : XReach k statics s) : KInv s ∧ KAux s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact h0
  | step _ hs ih =>
    cases hs with
    | kernel hs => exact hK _ _ ih.1 ih.2 hs
    | contentEnd hpre => exact contentEnd_preserves ih.1 ih.2 hpre

  cases o with

content.content:
## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes
## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root

**Static preconditions**

1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
2. **All leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.

**Outcomes**

# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)

Cette annexe décrit une **instance de bibliothèque** de la discipline MM-03, et non une nouvelle opération primitive du langage. Les noms sont sémantiques. Le contrat doit être reconstruit et vérifié ; les résultats du jalon 3 concernent le modèle exploratoire et ses conditions, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées ci-dessous.

## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage

Un handle est une donnée `(poolId, slot, gen)` **sans autorité d'accès intrinsèque**. L'identité logique `poolId` est fraîche et n'est pas réutilisée pendant l'exécution pertinente : détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle. Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite `{storage, internal, slots}`, où chaque slot possède `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`. Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage` ; leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets par l'implémentation de bibliothèque.

`storage` peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène. **`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage d'entrée soient `Uninit`** et doit vérifier la garde unifiée de MM-03.3 §2.7 bis sur les deux registres des abstractions vivantes. Il reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena` sans fabriquer ni droits ni initialisation des valeurs de slots. Les entrées libres sont `Uninit` ; leur génération initiale est zéro. Une autorité ne peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes, et une arène ne peut réutiliser l'`internal` d'un pool vivant.

## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution

Une résolution réussie dérive **de `internal` une autorité compagne** couvrant toutes les feuilles du stockage du pool, de mode `Observe` ou `Modify`, puis dérive **de cette compagne** une autorité de même mode par entrée résolue. L'autorité d'entrée est une descendante de la compagne, et non une autre dérivation indépendante de `internal`. Les deux sont soumises aux règles ordinaires de modes effectifs, d'exercice, de détention, d'ancrage et de transfert ; aucune permission nouvelle n'est créée.

`resolve(h, Observe | Modify)` vérifie l'identité de pool, la génération et la vivacité du slot **avant toute création d'autorité** : handle d'un autre pool, périmé, slot absent ou libre ⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état. Une résolution valide exige l'exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis. Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool ; des compagnes `Observe` peuvent coexister. Il est impossible de libérer une compagne tant que ses descendantes d'entrée sont actives (O3.2). La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau, pas seulement deux appels successifs de `resolve`.

`resolveMany(handles, Modify)` crée **une** compagne `Modify` et une autorité `Modify` par entrée. La distinction des slots est vérifiée dynamiquement pour ce lot ; toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**, sans création partielle de droits. `resolveMany(handles, Observe)` utilise des dérivations `Observe` de la compagne `Observe`, **sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction** : la répétition du même handle valide est permise. Les `reject` de discipline d'accès restent distincts des `fail` de validation des handles.

`unresolve` libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la compagne. Les règles de `release`, y compris celles qui empêchent la libération en présence de descendants ou d'ancres valides, restent applicables ; le contrat ne supprime pas silencieusement des autorités transférées.

## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot

`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige un pool vivant, l'autorisation d'administration de ses métadonnées, une destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active, non `Init`, apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle. `fail` si aucun slot libre ; `ok` choisit un slot libre, le rend vivant, conserve sa génération et écrit son handle dans la seule feuille `dst`, selon les obligations de représentation (Spec 4) et d'ABI (Spec 11). **Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit`** jusqu'à son écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot.

`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.

## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites

`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

Les générations sont des entiers naturels dans le modèle abstrait. Leur débordement ou leur recyclage dans une représentation finie doivent être empêchés par l'implémentation (par exemple retrait définitif d'un slot) ; l'ABI est spécifiée en Spec 11. L'encapsulation qui empêche un client d'accéder directement à une compagne administrative appartient à la Spec 9. Les handles persistants peuvent représenter des liens cycliques ; les résolutions qui en découlent restent temporaires et soumises à MM-03.

**Statut des preuves :** le jalon 3 rapporte `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct`, `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` et `pool_entries_disjoint` sur son brouillon, sous les hypothèses détaillées dans `J3_v0.1.md`. Il rapporte également un contre-exemple à l'ancienne formulation de `pool_inv_preserved`. **Il ne constitue pas encore la preuve** de la nouvelle règle `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight` ni de la totalité du contrat corrigé : ces obligations sont consignées en annexe F.

def Pool.entry (pl : Pool) : Arena.ArenaEntry := ⟨pl.storage, pl.internal, [], []⟩

/-- The shape of a pool (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; auxiliary; §38). -/
def Pool.shape (pl : Pool) : PoolShape := ⟨pl.id, pl.storage, pl.internal, pl.slots.map (·.place)⟩

/-- Updating a slot with the same place keeps the shape (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §38). -/
theorem setSlot_shape {pl : Pool} {i : Nat} {sl x : Slot} (hs : pl.slots[i]? = some sl)
    (hx : x.place = sl.place) : (setSlot pl i x).shape = pl.shape := by
  simp only [Pool.shape, setSlot, map_set_same (·.place) hs hx]

/-- Well-formedness of a pool shape (auxiliary, not a clause of the contract; HandlePool v0.4 annex,
HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1, from `newPool`): `internal` is a `Modify` authority whose footprint is
the footprint of the storage (§76.2, §76.3); the storage and every slot have a leaf; slots lie in
the storage and are pairwise disjoint (D.1). -/
structure PoolOK (s : S3) (sh : PoolShape) : Prop where
  /-- §76.2: `internal` exists, with own mode `Modify`. -/
  internalMode : OptP (s.A[sh.internal]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify) False
  /-- §76.3: `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`. -/
  fpEq : ∀ l, l ∈ s.afp sh.internal ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage
  /-- §40, §49.2: the storage has a leaf. -/
  storageLeaf : ∃ l, l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage
  /-- §40, §49.2: every slot has a leaf. -/
  slotLeaf : ∀ q ∈ sh.places, ∃ l, l ∈ footprint s.P q
  /-- D.1: slots lie in the storage. -/
  slotIn : ∀ q ∈ sh.places, ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage
  /-- D.1: slots are pairwise disjoint. -/
  disjoint : ∀ (a b qa qb : Nat), sh.places[a]? = some qa → sh.places[b]? = some qb → a ≠ b →
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P qa, l ∉ footprint s.P qb

/-- Well-formedness of a ghost resolution (auxiliary, HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2): it belongs to a
pool of `shs` with its `internal`; the companion is younger than `internal`, of the mode of the
resolution, over the footprint of the storage; each entry authority is younger than the companion,
over the footprint of its slot (§38, §60). -/
def ResOK (s : S3) (shs : List PoolShape) (r : Res) : Prop :=
  ∃ sh ∈ shs, sh.id = r.pool ∧ sh.internal = r.internal ∧ r.internal < r.comp ∧
    OptP (s.A[r.comp]?) (fun y => y.mode = r.mode ∧
      ∀ l, l ∈ y.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage) False ∧
    ∀ e ∈ r.entries, r.comp < e.1 ∧ ∃ q, sh.places[e.2.1]? = some q ∧
      OptP (s.A[e.1]?) (fun y => ∀ l, l ∈ y.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P q) False

/-- Ghost well-formedness of the pool layer (auxiliary, not a clause of the contract; HandlePool
v0.4 annex, D.1, D.2): fresh distinct identities, well-formed pools and
resolutions (§38). -/
structure PoolWF (L : PState) : Prop where
  /-- D.1: identities are below the next fresh identity. -/
  ids : ∀ sh ∈ L.pools.map Pool.shape, sh.id < L.nId
  /-- D.1: identities are distinct. -/
  nodup : ((L.pools.map Pool.shape).map (·.id)).Nodup
  /-- D.1: every pool is well formed. -/
  pools : ∀ sh ∈ L.pools.map Pool.shape, PoolOK L.kern sh
  /-- D.2: every ghost resolution is well formed. -/
  res : ∀ r ∈ L.res, ResOK L.kern (L.pools.map Pool.shape) r

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` as a state predicate (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2; non-normative
library contract): no active entry authority designates a free slot or a former generation (§89). -/
def NoStale (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ L.res, ∀ e ∈ r.entries, L.kern.Active e.1 → ∃ pl ∈ L.pools, pl.id = r.pool ∧
contract's sentence also covers the companions of other pools (`ModifyExclusive`). -/
def CompExcl (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → r₁.comp ≠ r₂.comp →
    L.kern.Active r₁.comp → L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .observe ∧ r₂.mode = .observe

/-- Footprints of every place with a leaf are kept (§40; support for HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
def FpKeep (s s' : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ q l₀, l₀ ∈ footprint s.P q → ∀ l, l ∈ footprint s'.P q ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P q

/-- Same places keep footprints (§40). -/
theorem fpKeep_of_P {s s' : S3} (h : s'.P = s.P) : FpKeep s s' := fun _ _ _ _ => by rw [h]

/-- Kernel steps keep footprints (§40; §60–§75 effects). -/
theorem fpKeep_kstep {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : KStep k s s') : FpKeep s s' :=
  fun _ _ h₀ l => Arena.kstep_fp h (Arena.footprint_lt h₀) l

/-- `FpKeep` composes (§40). -/
theorem FpKeep.trans {s s₁ s₂ : S3} (h₁ : FpKeep s s₁) (h₂ : FpKeep s₁ s₂) : FpKeep s s₂ :=

# fix4-pool: items B45 and B48 (blocking-report.md)

File edited: /Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern/formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean (only). Nothing committed. Branch unchanged.
Diff: 163 insertions, 121 deletions. With docstrings stripped, the code diff is exactly the B45 change below. Every other change is to a docstring.

## Clauses involved
- §49 (WF3), §50 (I1), §54 (NoDangling), §57 (main invariant), §69 (O12 effect).
- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3 (non-normative): "la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constitue une obligation explicite de reconstruction".
- Kernel pattern followed: commit a14dda0. It covers `EndFree.endUse_noDangling`, `endUse_preserves`, `endUse_preserves_kAux`, `EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux` and `Access.rootHeldConv_active` (Access/Lemmas.lean).

## B45: KAux removed from the KInv part

Statement diffs (old -> new):

- `contentEnd_noDangling`
  - old: `(hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s) (ha : RootHeldConv s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) (hw' : WF3 (endUseEff s q)) : NoDangling (endUseEff s q)`
  - new: `(hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s) (h1 : I1 s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) (hw' : WF3 (endUseEff s q)) : NoDangling (endUseEff s q)`
  - The proof calls `rootHeldConv_active hw h1 hnd j z l r hz₀ za hzo hlz hr hlr`, as `EndFree.endUse_noDangling` does.
- `contentEnd_preserves`
  - old: `(hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) : KInv (endUseEff s q) ∧ KAux (endUseEff s q)`
  - new: `(hk : KInv s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) : KInv (endUseEff s q)`
  - I1 is passed as `hk.2.1.1.1`.
- New `contentEnd_preserves_kAux {s : S3} {q : Nat} (ha : KAux s) : KAux (endUseEff s q)`
  - Proof: `EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux ha (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl`.
  - It takes no `ContentEndPre` hypothesis because the proof does not use it, the same as `EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux`. The statement is therefore for every `q`.
- `freeSlot_preserves`
  - old: `(hk : KInv L.kern) (ha : KAux L.kern) (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KInv L'.kern ∧ KAux L'.kern`
  - new: `(hk : KInv L.kern) (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KInv L'.kern`
- New `freeSlot_preserves_kAux (ha : KAux L.kern) (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KAux L'.kern`
  - It goes through `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` and `contentEnd_preserves_kAux`.
- `xreach_inv`: statement unchanged. Only the `contentEnd` case of the proof changed, to `⟨contentEnd_preserves ih.1 hpre, contentEnd_preserves_kAux ih.2⟩`.
- `freeSlot_not_endUse` (witness, near the old line :2018): unchanged.
  - It calls neither theorem; its `KInv ∧ KAux` facts are decided through `Arena.KInvB.sound`.
  - Its statement and its docstring ("Both states satisfy `KInv ∧ KAux`") describe its own conclusion, which is kept.

Docstrings updated:
- Module docstring (:23): `contentEnd_preserves` gives `KInv`; `contentEnd_preserves_kAux` gives the auxiliary `KAux` (not a clause of §57).
- Docstrings of `contentEnd_noDangling` (now cites `I1` §50 and `rootHeldConv_active`), `contentEnd_preserves`, `freeSlot_preserves` and `xreach_inv`.
- The duplicated "HandlePool v0.4 annex, HandlePool v0.4 annex" in the old `freeSlot_preserves` docstring is gone.
- `KernelGuarantee`'s docstring ("reduces it to the preservation of `KInv ∧ KAux` by every kernel step") is still accurate, because the statement of `xreach_inv` is unchanged. Left as is.
- No caller outside HandlePool.lean (checked with grep over formal/).

## B48: contract identifier in every docstring

- Two scripts:
  - Check: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/fix4pool/doccheck.py`. It lists every `/-- -/` docstring, the declaration kind it documents (def, theorem, structure, inductive, abbrev, instance, field) and whether it contains the literal "HandlePool v0.4 annex" or any mention of the annex.
  - Rewrite: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/fix4pool/apply_b48.py`. It applies explicit per-docstring texts, keyed by start line.
- Counts before (HEAD 6e56758 plus the B45 edit; 276 docstrings):
  - Literal "HandlePool v0.4 annex" missing: 53 def/theorem/structure/inductive/abbrev (25 def, 24 theorem, 3 inductive, 1 structure), which matches table E.
  - Also missing the literal: 3 instances and 23 documented structure fields, 79 in all.
  - No mention of the annex at all: 42 (24 def, 17 theorem, 1 inductive), which matches table E. Plus 3 instances and 23 fields: 68 in all.
- Counts after (278 docstrings, the 2 new theorems included): 0 missing the literal and 0 with no mention, in every kind, fields included.
- Item cited where one applies:
  - D.1: pool identity, storage, `internal`, the §56 guard, slot layout.
  - D.2: companion and entry authorities.
  - D.3: allocSlot, freeSlot and end of content, the slot write, and the HP-4 `freeSlot` subsection.
  - D.4: as already cited.
  - Generic helpers and initial witness states carry the identifier only: `KSeq`, `KSeq.trans`, `KSeq.single`, `XReach.kseq`, `optP_false_iff`, `chain_total`, `KSeq.keep`, `s3_ext`, `releaseEff_write3Eff`, `w0`, `n0`, `e0`, `g0`.
  - `fpKeep_of_P`, `fpKeep_kstep` and `FpKeep.trans` follow `FpKeep`'s existing wording: "support for HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1".
- 11 docstrings named the annex split across a line break ("HandlePool v0.4\nannex"). They were reflowed so the literal is on one line, with the wording unchanged.
- The `PoolOK` docstring had a duplicated "HandlePool v0.4 annex,\nHandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1"; the duplicate was removed.
- Non-normativity: the module docstring already states it ("**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex""). Unchanged.
- No new line exceeds 100 characters. The one 101-character line (`newPool(0, 8)` witness docstring, now :2291) was already there and was not touched.

## Checks
- `lake build` in formal/: "Build completed successfully (28 jobs)", with no line containing warn or error (log: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/fix4pool/build.log).
